question: If 6x = cosec θ and (6)/(x)=cot theta, then find the value of rm18(x²-(1)/(x²))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 6x = **cosec θ** and 6/x = **cot θ**

Square and subtract: (6x)² − (6/x)² = cosec² θ − cot² θ

36(x² − 1/x²) = 1

Divide by 2: 18(x² − 1/x²) = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a82c2291ff2d139e7da7e4028cf0d4b1e5e581c247b819fac2c74679d10ccfc1.png] 

**Given:**

x = (cosec θ)/6

1/x = (cot θ)/6

**Formula Used:**

Identity: **cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1**

**Calculations:**

⇒ x² = cosec² θ / 36

⇒ 1/x² = cot² θ / 36

⇒ (x² − 1/x²) = (cosec² θ − cot² θ) / 36

⇒ (x² − 1/x²) = 1 / 36

⇒ 18 × (x² − 1/x²) = 18 × (1 / 36)

⇒ 18(x² − 1/x²) = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

There are three primary identities: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Square Difference Property

In algebra, x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y), which is often combined with trig identities to simplify complex expressions.</p
